To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we cloned and sequenced the cDNA of the bifunctional enzyme dehydroquinase/shikimate dehydro-genase of Nicotiana taba-cum and that the amino acid sequence of the two catalytic domains of the enzyme is more closely related to that of prokaryotes than to that of yeast and fungi.
the N-terminal domain of the bifunctional enzyme is more closely related to bacterial dehydroquinases and the C-terminal domain is more closely related bacterial shikimate dehydratases.
a cDNA was cloned and sequented that encodes a bifunctional dehydrouinase/shikimate dehydrogease protein that complements E. coli aroD or aroE auxtrophs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning and characterization of the cDNA for the bifunctional protein dehydroquinase/shikimate dehydroginase (DHQ/SKDH) of aromatic amino acid biosynthesis.
the isolation and characterization of a cDNA encoding a dehydroquinase-shikimate dehydroganese (DHQ-SDH) bifunctional protein from Nicotiana tabaccum.
the isolation and characterization of a cDNA encoding a dehydroquinase/shikimate dehydroginase (DHQS) from Nicotiana tabaccum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bifunctional protein of Nicotiana tabacam has a greater amino acid identity to the homologues from prokaryotic species than to those from eukaryotic species.
the bifunctional protein is a member of a new family of enzymes.
the bifunctional enzyme of tobacco is more similar to the prokaryotic enzymes than to the yeast and fungal enzymes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cDNA was cloned from Nicotiana tabaccum, sequenced and found to encode a bifunctional dehyrogenase and a shikimate dehyrogenase.

the bifunctional enzyme of tobacco has a prokaryote-like catalytic domain for dehydroquinases and a eukaryote-like catalylic domain for shikimate dehydragenase, but that the N-terminal region of the mature protein, which is involved in the regulation of enzyme activity, has a prokayote-like structure.
the bifunctional protein of aromatic-amino acid biosynthesis in N. tabacum is encoded by a 2, 100 bp cDNA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single gene encodes the two enzymes in tobacco and that the two catalytic domains are separated by an N-terminal extension of about 50 residues.
the N. tabacum bifunctional protein is more similar to the prokaryote enzymes than the eukaryote enzymes.
the bifunctional enzyme is encoded by a single gene.
